title: The Museum Notebook
paragraphs: A museum volunteer invited a group of students to help prepare a notebook for visitors. The notebook would place brief observations beside the exhibits. Its purpose was to encourage careful attention: a reader should examine what happened before deciding what a scene might suggest.

The opening pages introduced several situations worth examining carefully. The new law will abolish the unfair fee completely. She chose to abstain from voting because she had a personal interest in the result. A shaded shelter helped alleviate the travelers' discomfort in the heat. The microphone will amplify your voice so everyone can hear it.

The remaining pages widened the discussion with additional observations. Students need time to assimilate new information and connect it with earlier learning. Quick repairs helped avert a serious accident on the bridge. The bully tried to coerce smaller children into giving him their lunch money. The security recording helped corroborate the witness's account.

When the group returned to its original question, the discussion had become more precise. The members could point to particular actions and details instead of relying on a vague impression. They did not force every account to teach the same lesson. Their final display invited readers to compare the evidence, explain a connection, and consider where that connection ended.

targets.definition: to formally end a law or practice
to deliberately choose not to do something
to take in and fully understand information
to prevent something bad from happening
to force someone through threats or pressure
to support a claim with additional evidence
